page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard1.36 is a bare-metal server belonging to the Standard family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon E5-2699 v3 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The hardware delivers 36 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core, yielding 72 dedicated vCPUs. System memory is provisioned at 256.0 GB, which corresponds to an allocation of 3.56 GB of memory per core thread.

Hardware accelerators are not included in this configuration, with a GPU count of zero. The platform also provisions no integrated local storage, requiring persistent storage needs to be handled via external network volumes. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Without hypervisor virtualization overhead, the instance delivers predictable, dedicated compute access. The balanced distribution of memory across a dense 72-vCPU pool makes this bare-metal machine cost-effective for scaled multithreaded operations. The configuration is well matched for general-purpose enterprise tasks, batch processing, continuous integration environments, and distributed application backends.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard1.36 is a dedicated bare-metal server configuration within the Standard family. Powered by Intel Xeon E5-2699 v3 processors on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 36 physical cores and 72 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 2.3 GHz. The platform is paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.56 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are not present, and the server includes no local storage drives, necessitating external network-attached volumes for data retention. Network provision includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. By eliminating hypervisor overhead on dedicated physical hardware with a balanced processor-to-memory allocation, BM.Standard1.36 serves as a balanced platform for standard enterprise computing, batch processing jobs, multi-threaded backend services, and continuous integration workloads requiring dedicated x86 execution capacity.
